bio_en: Mesrop Ter-Hakobian, known as Khanasortsi Mesrop, was the son of the priest Ter-Hakob of Alchamulk near Tabriz. After schooling in his village and at the Lilava school in Tabriz, he went on hunger strike until his parents sent him to the Etchmiadzin seminary. He then secretly bought a horse, rifle and cartridges, rode to Salmast and joined the ARF in late 1894, working on the preparations for the Khanasor expedition of 1897. He married in 1903, held many responsible posts during the Persian revolution of 1909-12, and died in Tabriz on 15 November 1915, barely forty.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. The text gives his birth as 1897, which is impossible given his death at 'barely 40' in 1915 - birth year left null.
